messages:
jess_support: Heads up — Acme (acme-dash-prod) opened a support ticket: repeated p95 token latency spikes and 429s on their Dedicated pool in eu-west-2c since ~21:10UTC. Seen across multiple model routes. Attaching short logs + request ids. :warning:
ryan_oncall: Can you paste the pool id, slice id, and a couple sample request_ids? Also, any recent autoscaler events? :eyes:
jess_support: pool_id=pool-eu2-acme, slice=acme-slice-7, sample_request_ids=[r-98f3, r-98f7]. Quick log snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T21:11:02Z] r-98f3 200ms gen start
[2026-03-16T21:11:11Z] r-98f3 ERROR 429 "slice capacity exceeded"
[2026-03-16T21:12:08Z] r-98f7 1.2s gen start
[2026-03-16T21:12:15Z] r-98f7 ERROR 429 "allocation failure: no free mig slot"
```
nik_infra: I pulled the cluster events for pool-eu2-acme. Autoscaler did two scale-up cycles at 21:09 and 21:13. Both attempted to add nodes but the scheduler reported fragmented MIG packing, leading to fractional leftover vGPU slots. Deploy bot shows: 
```
deploy-bot: autoscaler: attempted 3 launches, 2x failure (quota/fragmentation), final: succeeded with 1 node at 21:16
```
miguel_sre: That matches noisy-neighbor symptom where MIG partitioning + fractional packing causes jitter. Can you run a quick KV-cache heatmap and kvcache-hitrate for the slice? Also run a 5m trace with rdw-agent to capture scheduling latencies:
```
rdw-agent collect --span 5m --pool pool-eu2-acme --slice acme-slice-7 --output /tmp/acme-trace.tar
redwood metrics query "inference_p95{pool=\"pool-eu2-acme\",slice=\"acme-slice-7\"}[10m]"
```
jess_support: ran the metrics. p95 spiked from ~120ms to ~1.4s between 21:10-21:14. KV-cache hitrate dropped to 23% (normally ~78%). I uploaded trace: /tmp/acme-trace.tar and attached to ticket #T-45890. :link:
nik_infra: Inspecting MIG layout showed mixed slices (1g/2g/4g) on same host. Fractional leftover prevented autoscaler from placing the requested 2g vGPUs, leading to short-term 0 free_slots for acme. I also see high SM utilization from co-tenant tenant-x at same times.
miguel_sre: Repro suggestion for infra team: pack a test tenant to reproduce fragmentation by launching back-to-back 2g instances on a node with mixed existing allocations. Use this command to simulate allocation pressure:
```
redwoodctl reserve --pool pool-eu2-acme --mig 2g --count 6 --tag test-frag
```
ryan_oncall: Immediate mitigation: create an isolated slice for Acme (isolate remaining traffic) and shift routing. Can we move them to an existing reserved slice or create one small iso-slice? This should stop noisy neighbor hits while we debug packing logic. :thumbsup:
jess_support: I provisioned iso-slice-acme-20260316 and moved 30% of traffic at 21:19. Customer confirmed p95 dropped back to ~140ms and no new 429s since 21:22. I updated ticket T-45890 and notified customer.
nik_infra: Action items: 1) infra to run fragmentation repro in staging + adjust packer to prefer homogeneous MIG nodes (owner: nik_infra, ETA 48h). 2) autoscaler: add backoff/retry and smarter bin-packing to avoid temporary 0 free_slots (owner: miguel_sre, ETA 72h). 3) support: keep Acme on iso-slice until packer fix (owner: jess_support).
ryan_oncall: Also file an engineering follow-up to add an alert when kv-cache hitrate drops >50% from baseline and when autoscaler reports repeated fragmentation failures.
jess_support: Noted. I'll keep the thread updated with any customer feedback. Thanks all. :wave:
